items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: Well, there was a gentleman in my home town -- who Johnny Smith often speaks of, and I don't know whether he's alive or not, his name was Tom Robbins

ctx.x: He taught me -- I knew a little bit of the keyboard, so the xylophone was in the book, too, so they taught me the xylophone, and I got into practicing at home, but I lost interest in that, too, because of the upper registers of the violin key notes, you know, and I didn't put enough time in, and I was out all the time. But I did like popular music, which was coming along about 1928 or '29, like showboat songs and so on and so forth, and so I would buy sheet music and apply it to the four mallets of the xylophone.

Well, there was a gentleman in my home town -- who Johnny Smith often speaks of, and I don't know whether he's alive or not, his name was Tom Robbins, and he was a kind of, well, erratic sort of person, but he had a basic -- he used to write strange tales, among other things. But he played the x the guitarist
banjo -- he wrote a lot of banjo, he was in all those things in the twenties, he was a banjo virtuoso, and he was also a very strange person.
